source: Heifer Cambodia -- Cattle Feed and Feeding Guide (2006)
text:
If a cow is fed daily but still not gaining weight, the most common underlying reason is that feed quantity does not equal feed quality. Rice straw, the staple dry-season feed for most Cambodian cattle, is very low in protein (about 3.5%) and low in digestibility, so straw alone cannot support real weight gain regardless of quantity eaten.

Practical fixes: treat rice straw with urea to raise digestibility and protein value; supplement with protein-rich local leaves (cassava leaves, leucaena leaves); add rice bran (2-4 kg/day, supplies energy, protein, calcium, phosphorus); or use a molasses-urea lick block for cheap energy and usable nitrogen.

Water intake is a frequently overlooked cause of poor weight gain -- inadequate water reduces feed intake and digestion; a dehydrated animal can lose roughly 16% of body weight and shows rough coat, dull eyes, restlessness. Water needs rise sharply with heat: below 20C, cattle need roughly 4-5 liters per kg of dry feed; above 30C (common in Cambodia's hot season), this rises to 10-12 liters per kg of dry feed.

Mineral deficiencies (phosphorus, calcium, sulfur, copper, zinc) independently cause slowed growth and poor feed efficiency even with adequate bulk feed -- a simple mineral or salt block is a low-cost troubleshooting step.

Internal parasites (including liver fluke/Fasciola, a documented concern in Cambodian cattle) and underlying disease can also cause poor weight gain despite adequate feeding -- regular deworming and a livestock officer check are worth ruling out if feed and water are already adequate.
